# IEA "Key Questions on Energy and AI" (2026) — Executive summary

IEA (2026), *Key Questions on Energy and AI*, IEA, Paris. Follow-up to the April 2025 *Energy and AI* report.

## Key figures
- Largest tech companies' capital expenditure exceeded USD 400 billion in 2025, expected to jump another 75% in 2026. Capex of just five tech companies is now larger than global investment in oil and natural gas production.
- IEA satellite-based tracking: "AI factories" (cutting-edge data centres designed for AI) have more than tripled in capacity in the past 18 months.
- Energy use per AI task dropping by at least an order of magnitude annually. If all conventional internet searches were done as simple AI text queries: less than 4 TWh annually, <1% of total data centre consumption today.
- New energy-intensive AI applications (video generation, reasoning, agentic tasks) can consume hundreds or thousands of times more energy per query than simple text generation.
- Global data centre electricity demand grew 17% in 2025; AI-focused data centres grew 50% in 2025. Major model providers: 3x active users, 5x revenue over the past year.
- Updated projection: data centre electricity consumption roughly doubles from 485 TWh in 2025 to 950 TWh in 2030 (~3% of global electricity demand). AI-focused data centre consumption triples in this period.
- By 2027 a single AI server rack could have peak power demand equivalent to 65 households; AI server power density increased 11x between 2020 and 2025, set to increase another 4x by 2027.
- By 2030, ~20–25 GW of battery storage could be installed in data centres globally.
- US: ~one-fifth of onsite gas data centre projects have started land clearing/construction. Reliable onsite gas requires overbuilding onsite generation by 30–70% relative to demand. ~15–27 GW of onsite natural gas may power data centres by 2030, mostly in the US.
- AI-driven growth boost could raise global energy demand by 1–4% in 2035. AI-enabled optimisation could reduce energy costs by 3–10 percentage points in energy-intensive industries; >13 EJ saved by 2035 (~3% of global final energy consumption).
- Data centre emissions double in IEA projections to ~350 million tonnes in 2035, ~2% of global electricity sector emissions.
- 70% surge in gas turbine orders in 2025.
- Only 10% of global electricity consumption is covered by open electricity data policies.
